acilis-bilgi: The Nutuk is the great speech Mustafa Kemal Atatürk delivered in 1927, telling the story of the National Struggle and the founding of the Republic, and it opens with these words. This map tells that journey through its turning points, from 16 May 1919 to 29 October 1923. Source: Nutuk–Söylev, I. Cilt, s. 2, T.C. Kültür ve Turizm Bakanlığı e-kitap (ekitap.ktb.gov.tr). Quotations from the Nutuk are translated for this site; the original Turkish is shown with each.
acilis-kimden: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, Nutuk (The Great Speech, 1927) · “1919 senesi Mayısının 19 uncu günü Samsun'a çıktım.”
acilis-soz: On the 19th day of May 1919, I landed at Samsun.

hk-giris: The turning points and journeys of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk from his departure from İstanbul on 16 May 1919 to the proclamation of the Republic on 29 October 1923.

hk-kunye-metin: Prepared by: Mehmet Ali Yanmaz · georehber.com · Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) · Routing: OSRM · Country borders: Natural Earth · Basemap: Esri Light Gray Canvas and World Hillshade; in the 3D view Esri World Imagery and terrain elevation · Narration: Adam Stone (ElevenLabs) · Fonts: Lora, Inter (SIL Open Font License) · Colours: Okabe-Ito palette, colour-blind friendly · Tools: Claude, Python, ArcGIS Online, ArcGIS Maps SDK for JavaScript
hk-nasil-liste:
• The map shows the turning points of the period and the journeys connecting them. The account and photographs for each stop are in the stop card.
  • "Continue the journey" at the bottom of the card moves to the next stop, and the route is drawn on the map as you go; "Previous stop" goes back. You can also tap the icons on the timeline to go to a stop.
  • The icon of the current stop is outlined with a thin orange line and shown in full colour, earlier ones faded; the most recently drawn route is the most prominent. Where a city has several stops, only the latest one is shown on the map.
  • The colour of a route shows how he travelled; each card says so under "How he got here". Where the sources do not say, the line is grey. The colours come from the colour-blind friendly Okabe-Ito palette. The legend button at the top left explains the icons and colours.
  • "Watch the journey" at the bottom left plays the whole journey in 3D from the beginning: the camera follows the route, a vehicle moves along it, and at each stop one or two narrated sentences tell what happened there while a model marking the event appears. Zooming in with the + and − buttons or the mouse wheel makes the vehicle smaller and slower; zooming out makes it larger and faster. Where the means of travel is unknown, the vehicle is semi-transparent.
hk-yollar-metin: The roads of those years no longer exist; the lines follow today's road and railway equivalents of the same route. Sea routes are approximate. The steamer, car and train in the 3D view are models evoking the vehicles of the period, and the buildings and objects at the stops are representations; a vehicle's position on the route is estimated from the start and end dates of the journey.
lejant-not: Lines follow today's equivalent of the route. The emphasised line is the latest journey; faded lines are earlier routes.
